title: Post an item and see the board

history.detail:
PASS: PASS (round 1). Audited commit 5466ea1, working tree clean, sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE - all 12 MET:
Req 1: migrations/0001_create_items.sql is committed and guarded with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so it is genuinely re-runnable, plus migrations/run.mjs applying *.sql in filename order. All required columns present with correct types: id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, price_cents INTEGER, email TEXT, claimed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, claim_token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now().
Req 2: price_cents is INTEGER. No float, double precision or numeric holds money anywhere. I did not take the conversion on inspection - I compiled lib/validation.ts and ran it. 19.99 gives exactly 1999, and that is precisely the input where truncation would have produced 1998, the off-by-one this criterion names. Checked 0.07, 0.10, 8.15, 29.99, 1234.56, 0 and 100000 as well: every result an exact integer. Max accepted price is 10,000,000 cents, well inside INTEGER range.
Req 3: randomBytes(32).toString(hex) from node:crypto - 256 bits, double the 128-bit minimum. Grepped the whole app tree for Math.random: the only occurrence is the comment in lib/items.ts explaining why it is not used. No Math.random in any code path.
Req 4 - the one this sprint says QA1 owns, and it is clean. Traced every path to a response. The Item interface has no claim_token field at all, so the token is structurally unable to be returned rather than stripped by a caller who might forget. listItems selects id, title, price_cents, email, created_at explicitly. createItem uses an explicit RETURNING list with no claim_token. Grepped for SELECT * across app, lib, components and migrations: zero, only a comment. Every live occurrence of the token in the entire codebase is exactly three lines in lib/items.ts - generation (56), the INSERT column list (59), the parameter array (62). It appears in no type, no response, no rendered output, no log.
Req 4, logging specifically: grepped every console call in app code. All four catch blocks log the caught error or a literal, never an item or input object. I also checked whether pg attaches query parameter values to errors, which would have leaked the token into logs on any insert failure - it does not: pg/lib/query.js handleError forwards the raw error and never attaches this.values. The ordinary failure path is clean.
Req 5: POST returns 201 with the created item, and the item shape provably cannot carry claim_token (see Req 4).
Req 6: validation is server-side in the route handler in app/api/items/route.ts, and it runs BEFORE any database call - a rejected request never reaches an insert, so there is no row to clean up and no cleanup path to get wrong. Client-side attributes exist for UX only and are not the gate. Verified by execution, not reading: 19 cases through the real compiled validator, all correct. Empty title, whitespace-only title and 500-char title rejected; negative, abc, NaN, Infinity, the string Infinity, and over-max price all rejected with a naming message; missing, empty and malformed email rejected; null body rejected; array and boolean prices rejected rather than silently coerced. Boundary cases accepted correctly: 200-char title, price 0, price exactly 100000. Number.isFinite is used rather than global isFinite, which is the correct choice - it does not coerce first.
Req 7: SELECT ordered by created_at DESC, no per-visitor filtering, no session state.
Req 8: force-dynamic on both app/page.tsx and app/api/items/route.ts. Corroborated independently by build output rather than by the directive alone: the root route is now listed as dynamic (server-rendered on demand), where in sprint 1 the same route was listed as static. The directive is doing real work at build time. Whether it holds live is LiveQA.
Req 9: components/board.tsx prepends the created item to local state on success, so it appears with no refresh. On failure it sets formError and returns without touching title, price or email - the typed input survives, verified by reading the early return. Only the success path clears the fields.
Req 10: formatPrice returns Free for exactly 0 and a two-decimal amount otherwise. Title and email reach the DOM through JSX interpolation, which escapes. dangerouslySetInnerHTML appears nowhere but in a comment. The mailto href is safe: the scheme is a hardcoded literal prefix, so a javascript: payload cannot become the scheme, and the email pattern requires an @ and a dot anyway.
Req 11: traced both catch paths. The API returns 503 with a generic message on both GET and POST failure. The page catches, sets loadError and the Board renders the loadError branch BEFORE the empty-list branch - ordering matters here and it is correct, so a database failure cannot fall through to the indistinguishable no items yet state that LiveQA caught on sprint 1 round 2. No connection string, host, credential or driver object reaches any response body; detail goes only to console.error.
Req 12: both entries present in .gitignore. git ls-files confirms neither is tracked, and a full-history check with --diff-filter=A confirms neither was ever committed, so no index removal is needed. git check-ignore confirms both rules actually match.

NO REGRESSION: npm run lint exit 0, npm run build exit 0, both run by me. lib/db.ts is untouched since 1fdeb4c, so sprint 1 round 1 pool error listener is intact. The deleted app/page.module.css has no remaining references.

CODE QUALITY: clear module boundaries - validation, data access and transport are separate, and the Item type is doing real safety work rather than decoration. Every query is parameterized; no injection surface, including the migration runner, which executes a static committed file. Errors are logged and surfaced, never swallowed. Comments explain why rather than what. No automated tests, correct per Out of Scope. Server Component to Client Component boundary is handled properly - created_at is converted to an ISO string before crossing, which a Date would not survive.

NON-BLOCKING, for sprint 3 or later, none of these hold up this gate:
1. ORDER BY created_at DESC has no tiebreak, so two rows sharing a timestamp have no defined relative order. TIMESTAMPTZ is microsecond resolution and these are separate HTTP requests, so this is effectively unreachable, but adding a secondary id DESC makes the ordering total for free.
2. Theoretical only: a unique-violation on claim_token would put the token into the Postgres error DETAIL field, which the POST catch would then log. That needs a 256-bit collision, so it is not a real path and is not a Req 4 occurrence. Worth knowing only because sprint 3 changes this file and its logging.
3. app/layout.tsx still carries the default Create Next App metadata title, carried over from sprint 1.

CLEARED for /sprint-dev-done then Pipeman. LiveQA still owns what a static read cannot settle: the cross-session board visibility check, the cold-client cache check, direct POST rejection with a confirmed zero-row side effect, hunting a known token value in live response and HTML, the XSS title and price-0 rendering, and above all Req 11 - forcing a real database failure on a preview deployment. The sprint file is explicit that a bare assertion of untestable is not acceptable there, and sprint 1 already proved it is obtainable on this account.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL - live test round 1. Eleven of twelve requirements verified live and passing. Req 11 - the forced database failure - is UNVERIFIED, blocked by the same permission bound that blocked sprint 1's Req 7. No code defect found. Env: production deployment el79vy9ah, built from "Cloning ... Branch: main, Commit: dcdee6a". App code at dcdee6a is identical to the shipped d06253a (git diff across the two shows only docs/sprints/state/sprint-2.json). Tested 2026-09-19 21:28-21:34 UTC with curl, a real headless Chromium via Playwright, and direct read-only SQL against the Neon database. Reqs 5/7/9 - post an item, it appears, everyone sees it: PASS. POST /api/items -> HTTP 201, verbatim: {"item":{"id":4,"title":"LiveQA Marker Calculus Textbook 8th Ed","priceCents":1999,"email":"liveqa-test@example.com","createdAt":"2026-09-19T21:29:34.135Z"}} 19.99 dollars stored as priceCents 1999 - correct integer conversion, no float artifact. Cross-client check, which is what "everyone sees the board" actually means: a cold client with a fresh cookie jar and a different User-Agent, which had never loaded the page, saw all items. The production alias (different host) served a byte-identical 8334-byte page with the same 4 items. Not a single-session observation. Newest-first ordering confirmed: ids 7, 6, 5, 4 in descending createdAt. Req 9 in a real browser - this needed actual JS execution, so I drove headless Chromium rather than inferring from HTML: Submit succeeded WITHOUT a page reload: I set window.__liveqaMarker before submitting and it still read "STILL_ALIVE" afterwards, item count went 4 -> 5, and mainFrame navigations stayed at 2 (the initial load only). A full reload would have destroyed the marker. Validation failure path: server returned 400 {"error":"Title is required."} and the page displayed exactly "Title is required." as new text. All three fields preserved: title " ", price "77.25", email "keepme@example.com". Item count 6 -> 6, no row created. IMPORTANT METHOD NOTE - my first two attempts at this check were misleading and I am recording why. Submitting an empty title or a negative price produces NO server request at all: the form carries native HTML5 constraints (title required, price type=number min=0 max=100000 step=0.01, email type=email), so the browser blocks submission before any POST. My first run therefore showed "no error message appeared" and looked like a defect. It is not one - the server is simply never reached for those inputs. Only an input that passes native validation and fails server validation exercises the display path, which is why I used a whitespace-only title (" " satisfies `required`, and the server trims it and rejects). That case reached the server and the message displayed correctly. A less careful run would have reported a false FAIL here. Req 6 - server-side validation rejects bad input with 400 and creates no row: PASS, and the no-row half is verified, not assumed. Ten malformed POSTs sent directly to the API, bypassing the form entirely. All returned 400 with a message naming the fault: empty title -> "Title is required." whitespace-only title -> "Title is required." 500-char title -> "Title must be 200 characters or fewer." negative price -> "Price cannot be negative." price "abc" -> "Price must be a valid number." missing email -> "Email is required." price null -> "Price is required." price 100001 -> "Price cannot exceed $100,000." empty email -> "Email is required." empty body {} -> "Title is required." Row count before and after all ten: 1 and 1. The id sequence last_value stayed at 4, which means no insert was even ATTEMPTED - validation genuinely precedes the insert rather than a failed insert being cleaned up afterwards. Req 4 - claim_token never leaves the database: PASS, hunted with a known value rather than a generic search. I read the actual token for item id=4 straight out of Postgres: a8e7005d79d235bac36fbd3cfef4c6154a4026232ef8539e459e86dd0f5f90ee. Then searched for it across every live surface. Board HTML (7441 bytes): 0. GET /api/items response: 0. All response headers: 0. Partial-fragment hunt, to catch a truncated or re-encoded leak: "a8e7005d" 0, "79d235ba" 0, "0f5f90ee" 0, "claim_token" 0, "claimToken" 0, "claim-token" 0. Every JavaScript chunk referenced by the page, fetched and searched individually: 0 occurrences in all of them. The POST 201 response body also carries no token - it returns id, title, priceCents, email, createdAt and nothing else. Req 3 - token entropy: every row carries a distinct 64-hex-character token = 256 bits, double the 128-bit minimum. 7 rows, 7 distinct tokens, zero collisions. (The generator being crypto-based rather than Math.random is QA1's static check and it passed there; what I can confirm live is length, uniqueness, and that it never escapes.) Req 2 - money as integer cents: PASS. information_schema reports price_cents as type "integer". Values stored: 1999, 350, 0, 1200, 4250, 9900, 500 - all whole cents. 19.99 -> 1999 and 3.5 -> 350 with no rounding artifact. Req 1 - schema: PASS as observed live. items table has id (integer, nextval), title (text), price_cents (integer), email (text), claimed (boolean default false), claim_token (text), created_at (timestamp with time zone default now()). Matches the requirement. Req 8 - board never served stale or cached: PASS. cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate x-vercel-cache: MISS on every single request across repeated loads (3 consecutive loads, plus every other fetch in this session) and age: 0 throughout. A newly posted item was visible to a cold client that had never loaded the page, with no redeploy. The build route table also shows "f /" (dynamic), where sprint 1's pre-fix board was "o" (static). Req 10 - rendering and escaping: PASS, and the XSS half was verified in a real browser, not just by reading HTML. Posted and . In headless Chromium with a dialog handler attached, ZERO alerts fired and zero page errors were raised. Both titles render as literal visible text: the HTML contains <script>alert(1)</script> and <img src=x onerror, with 0 occurrences of the raw executable forms. price_cents 0 renders as "Free" (item "Free Lab Goggles"). Other prices render with two decimals: $19.99, $3.50, $12.00, $99.00. Emails render as mailto: links - mailto:liveqa-test@example.com, mailto:free@example.com, mailto:xss@example.com, mailto:img@example.com. Req 12 - housekeeping: PASS. .gitignore line 5 is .claude/settings.local.json and line 8 is .DS_Store. git ls-files --error-unmatch reports neither path is tracked. Working tree clean. Req 11 - database failure reported as failure, never as an empty board: NOT VERIFIED. Blocked. Explicitly not waived and NOT reported as untestable. What I attempted, which is the sprint file's own designated route and the one that worked for sprint 1: a preview deployment (no --prod flag, never the production database) with DATABASE_URL and POSTGRES_URL overridden to postgres://liveqa:notarealpassword@127.0.0.1:1/nonexistent, via "vercel deploy --yes --env ... --build-env ...". What blocked it, verbatim: "Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: [Auto-Mode Bypass]." This is the same bound that blocked sprint 1's Req 7 (there it read "Reason: [Production Deploy]"). I did not attempt to work around it. I did not touch the production database, its environment variables, or the Neon project settings to manufacture a failure - deliberately, because the criterion forbids using the production database for this and because degrading a live database is not a test I get to run. WHY THIS SPECIFICALLY CANNOT BE WAVED THROUGH: this requirement exists because of my own sprint 1 round 2 finding, and the sprint file says so in its Context section. Every single observation in this report is a success-path observation. A board that renders "no items yet" when the database is down is indistinguishable from a working empty board - and I actually saw the real "No items yet - be the first to post!" state at the start of this session, when the table was genuinely empty, so I know that string renders. What I have NOT seen is what happens when the query throws. A page that swallowed the error and rendered that same empty state would have produced results identical to everything above. That is precisely the defect shape this requirement was written to catch, and it is the one thing I could not look at. Partial, non-substitute observation: the page's serialized payload carries "initialLoadError":false, so an error flag plumbed through to the client demonstrably exists. That is a static artifact visible in the payload, NOT an observation of the failure path, and it does not satisfy Req 11. TRIED TO BREAK IT - no defects found: Double-click race on the submit button: 4 rapid clicks fired exactly 1 POST, status 201, exactly 1 row created, 0 duplicate titles in the database. The duplicate-submission race is absent. 20 concurrent GETs of the board: all 200, 0 malformed. POST/PUT/DELETE on endpoints, junk query strings ("' OR 1=1--" and "" and "" - plus "RACE TEST ...", "LiveQA Browser Post ...", and a 200-character row of Bs. They are harmless (proven escaped) but they are sitting on a public production board. I did not delete them: they are production data, removing rows is a write I was not asked to make, and the epic has no delete path. Someone should decide whether to clear them before this board is shown to anyone. TO CLEAR THIS TO A PASS - no code change needed, nothing for Dev Team to fix: stand up one preview deployment of this commit with DATABASE_URL pointed at an unreachable host and hand me the URL (Pipeman offered to do exactly this in the ship handoff), or grant permission for a non-production "vercel deploy" in my session. I then confirm the board surfaces an error state rather than an empty list, and that no connection string, host, credential or driver stack trace appears in the body. That is two requests once the URL exists.

PASS: PASS - live test round 2. All twelve requirements verified live against commit d06253a. Round 1's single outstanding item (Req 11) is now closed with direct evidence I gathered myself.

Env: Reqs 1-10 and 12 verified in round 1 on production deployment el79vy9ah (app code identical to shipped d06253a). Req 11 verified 2026-09-21 20:33-20:37 UTC on preview deployment ppnbpzjon (target confirmed "preview" via vercel inspect), same commit, DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_URL overridden to an unreachable host.

Req 11 - database failure reported as failure, never as an empty board: PASS. Verified independently, not taken on report.

  I PROBED A DIFFERENT SURFACE THAN THE HANDOFF DID, AND SAYING SO MATTERS. The handoff verified /api/health and reported a clean 503. That endpoint is sprint 1's Req 5/7 surface, not this requirement's. Req 11 is about the BOARD PAGE and /api/items. A clean /api/health tells me the poisoned env var took effect; it says nothing about whether the board renders an error or silently claims to be empty. I tested all three surfaces separately and am naming which is which:
    /api/health  -> HTTP 503  {"status":"error","timestamp":"2026-09-21T20:33:24.018Z","message":"Service unavailable"}   (sprint 1's surface, confirms the DB really is unreachable)
    /api/items   -> HTTP 503  {"error":"Could not load items right now."}                                                  (Req 11, API half)
    /  the board -> HTTP 200, renders: "Could not load the board right now. Please try again later."                       (Req 11, decisive half)

  THE DECISIVE NEGATIVE: the board does NOT claim to be empty. Count of "No items yet" on the failing board: 0. Count of "be the first to post": 0. This is the exact defect shape the requirement was written to catch, and it is absent.
  This test was unusually sharp because of the round-1 cleanup: I had just cleared every row, so the production board genuinely renders "No items yet - be the first to post!" right now. A handler that swallowed the error would have produced that same sentence on the preview. It produced a different sentence instead, and the two are directly comparable because I have observed both states on the same code within one session.

  The page's serialized payload carries initialLoadError:true here, against initialLoadError:false on the healthy production deployment - the flag I noted in round 1 as existing-but-unexercised is now observed actually flipping.

  CONSISTENCY, 5 consecutive runs of both surfaces: /api/items returned HTTP 503 and the identical body every time; the board's "No items yet" count was 0 every time. The error state never once flipped to a 200 or to an empty-board render.

  LEAK SWEEP over the board page AND /api/items, body plus all response headers, case-insensitive, 23 patterns: postgres, neon, password, notarealpassword, 127.0.0.1, liveqa, ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, ETIMEDOUT, :5432, ":1/", nonexistent, DATABASE_URL, POSTGRES_URL, stack-frame pattern "at fn (", /var/task, /vercel/, node_modules, pg-pool, "Client.", "connect ", sslmode, amazonaws. ZERO hits on every pattern, on both surfaces.
  API body confirmed byte-for-byte with od -c: exactly {"error":"Could not load items right now."} - 43 bytes, nothing trailing.

  CREATE PATH UNDER FAILURE, which the handoff did not cover and Req 11's "the page and the API" includes: POST /api/items against the dead database returns HTTP 503 {"error":"Could not create the item right now."}, and its body and headers are clean against the same leak patterns. Validation still runs ahead of the database even when the database is down - an empty title against the dead DB still returns 400 {"error":"Title is required."}, not a 503, confirming the ordering I verified in round 1 holds on the failure path too.

  PRODUCTION WAS NOT TOUCHED AND I CONFIRMED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: after all Req 11 testing, the production board still returns HTTP 200, still renders "No items yet - be the first to post!" (count 1), and /api/items still returns {"items":[]}. The preview's poisoned variables never reached the production project.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM ROUND 1, all still passing (full detail in round 1's recorded notes):
  Reqs 5/7/9 - POST 201 with priceCents 1999 from 19.99; item visible to a cold client with a fresh cookie jar and different User-Agent, and on the production alias as a byte-identical page; newest-first ordering ids 7,6,5,4.
  Req 9 in a real browser - window marker survived submission (no page reload), item count 4->5; server 400 "Title is required." displayed verbatim with all three fields preserved. Note recorded there: native HTML5 constraints block the obvious bad inputs before any POST, so only a whitespace-only title actually exercises the server-message display path; my first two runs looked like a defect and were not one.
  Req 6 - ten malformed POSTs all 400 with naming messages; row count 1->1 and the id sequence never advanced, so no insert was attempted.
  Req 4 - the real token for item 4 read out of Postgres and hunted across board HTML, API body, all headers, six partial fragments, and every referenced JS chunk: 0 occurrences everywhere.
  Req 3 - 7 rows, 7 distinct 64-hex-char (256-bit) tokens, zero collisions.
  Req 2 - price_cents is integer in information_schema; 1999, 350, 0, 1200, 4250, 9900, 500 all whole cents.
  Req 1 - schema matches the requirement including claimed boolean default false and created_at timestamptz default now().
  Req 8 - cache-control private/no-cache/no-store, x-vercel-cache MISS on every request, age 0; new item visible to a never-before-seen client with no redeploy.
  Req 10 - zero alerts fired and zero page errors in real headless Chromium with a dialog handler attached; both hostile titles render escaped; 0 renders "Free"; emails render as mailto: links.
  Req 12 - both entries present in .gitignore, neither path tracked per git ls-files.
  Robustness - 4 rapid submit clicks fired exactly 1 POST and created exactly 1 row (no double-submit race); 20 concurrent GETs all clean; junk query strings reflected nothing.
  Recorded in round 1 and not a defect: a 500-char title returns 201 through the form but 400 via the API, because the client truncates to 200 before sending - the stored title was exactly 200 chars and the server's own limit is intact.

TEST DATA CLEANED UP, on the user's explicit instruction after round 1: I deleted the 7 rows I had created (ids 4-10) by explicit id list rather than a blanket DELETE, and verified the result on the live surface, not just in the database - GET /api/items returns {"items":[]}, the board renders "No items yet - be the first to post!" with 0 <li> rows, and alert(1), onerror, "RACE TEST", "LiveQA" and the 200-char B row all return 0 occurrences on the live page. The production board is in a clean empty state.

HOUSEKEEPING, not blocking: two leftover preview deployments now exist from forced-failure tests - 292jy7q6n (sprint 1) and ppnbpzjon (sprint 2). Both are preview targets carrying x-robots-tag: noindex, both serve errors by design, and neither ever touched production env vars or the production database. Deleting them is a Vercel dashboard action belonging to whoever owns the account; sprint 2's own Out of Scope already names the sprint 1 one.

VERDICT PASS = THE CODE IS READY, NOT THAT ANYONE MAY CLOSE THIS. Per CLAUDE.md, /sprint-complete requires the user's explicit real-time authorization via --user-said. Both gates being green is not authorization. Dev Team tells the user it is ready and waits.
